title: HSK 2 · Stories
description: Fifty short stories with a little more room — 得 complements, 因为/所以, past experience.

sentences.en: I have a very old bicycle.
It's red, though the color has faded now.
Every morning I ride it to work.
It goes slowly, but I don't want to sell it.

tokens.en: (links a verb to how it is done)

sentences.en: I feel it's a friend of mine.
Last year I still couldn't swim.
I found the water very frightening.
My friend said: don't be afraid, I'll help you.
We went twice a week.
Now I swim quite fast.

tokens.en: (links a verb to how it is done)

passages.title: 找不到的狗
passages.title_en: The Dog That Couldn't Be Found

sentences.en: Last night my dog went out.
I looked next to the house for an hour.
It was dark outside, and cold.
When I got home, it was sleeping by the door.
It saw me and was delighted.
Last week we had a Chinese exam.
I prepared for a long time.
There were a lot of questions and I wrote slowly.

tokens.en: (links a verb to how it is done)

sentences.en: I didn't have time for the last question.
The teacher said I did all right.

tokens.en: (links a verb to how it is done)

sentences.en: When I got up this morning, everything outside was white.
It had snowed all night.
There were no cars on the road, and no people.
I walked a long way in the snow by myself.
I think it was the best morning of the year.
My brother's phone is new and expensive.
He looks at it all day, even while eating.

sentences.en: Mom says this isn't good for him.
Last week his phone broke.
For those three days he talked with us a lot.
Tomorrow is my little sister's birthday; she's turning seven.
I want to give her something, but I don't have much money.

sentences.en: I think she'd like a card I wrote myself.
On it I wrote five characters: happy birthday, little sister.
When she saw it she smiled.
Last summer our family went travelling.
We took a ten-hour train.
The ride was tiring, but also great fun.
We saw big mountains and a long river.
This year I want to go again.
Next to my house there's a red door.
That door is always closed.
I asked my mom what was inside.
She said she didn't know either.
Now I glance at it every time I walk past.

tokens.en: to look at; to read; to watch

sentences.en: The doctor said I should exercise more.
So I started running.
The first day I ran ten minutes and was exhausted.
My friend said: go slower, but go longer.
Now I run half an hour a day.
I drink two cups of coffee every morning.
My wife says that's too much coffee.
Last month I went a week without any.
That week I was tired every day and didn't feel like talking.
Now I have one cup a day.
When I was little I lived in a very small room.
There was only a bed and a table in it.
But outside the door there was a big tree.
Every morning I heard the birds in that tree.
My room now is big, but there's no tree.
Yesterday I took the train to work.
The man next to me slept the whole way.
His book fell on the floor.
I woke him and he said thank you.
Getting off, he forgot the book.
My favorite color is red.
A lot of my clothes are red.
My little sister likes white best.
She says white is clean.
Mom says: white clothes have to be washed often.
My cat can open doors.
It uses its head and opens them slowly.
At five in the morning it comes into my room.
It sits on me to make me get up.
I think I need a new door.
Last week I got sick.
I didn't go to work for three days.
My colleague called to ask how I was.
She also brought over medicine and fruit.

sentences.en: I'm better now, and I want to take her to dinner.
Tonight I'm the only one at home.
It's raining outside and very quiet.
I washed clothes and made an egg.
Then I watched a very old film.

tokens.en: to look at; to read; to watch

sentences.en: I think an evening alone is nice too.
My teacher gave me a Chinese name.
She said the name means "happy mountain".
I like it very much.
But I don't write it well.

tokens.en: (links a verb to how it is done)

sentences.en: So I write it ten times a day.

passages.title: 学校旁边的小店
passages.title_en: The Little Shop by the School

sentences.en: There's a little shop next to our school.
Everything in it is cheap.
After class the students all go there for milk.
The old man in the shop knows every student.
He also knows what each of us likes.
I'm not afraid of studying, but I'm very afraid of tests.
On the morning of a test I can't eat anything.
My friend says he's the same.
The teacher says: a test is only a piece of paper.
I know she's right, but I'm still afraid.

tokens.en: (links a verb to how it is done)

sentences.en: My dad has a very old watch.
His father gave it to him.
It doesn't keep good time — five minutes slow a day.

tokens.en: (links a verb to how it is done)

sentences.en: I said: buy a new one.
He said: this watch remembers a lot of things.
Our math teacher never smiles.
Last week a classmate got a question wrong.
His answer was very funny.
The teacher smiled, and we all saw it.
After that day none of us were afraid of her.
I like the city at night.
There are fewer cars and fewer people.
The lights on the road are all yellow.
I often walk a long way by myself.
When I'm tired I take the bus home.
Last month my friend's older sister got married.
Everyone was dancing.
I can't dance, so I sat to the side and ate.
A little child came and made me dance with her.
She didn't dance well either, and we both laughed.

tokens.en: (links a verb to how it is done)

sentences.en: My first job was at a small restaurant.
Every day I washed a lot of cups.
My hands were wet all the time.
But everyone there was very good to me.
I still remember that restaurant's food.
A young person lives in the room next to mine.
He listens to music every night.
At first I was very unhappy about it.
But now I like that music too.
Yesterday he didn't play any, and it felt too quiet.
Last Wednesday was my busiest day.
I started work at eight and didn't get home until ten.
At noon I only ate one egg.
By the time I got home I was too tired to speak.

tokens.en: (links a verb to how it is done)

sentences.en: But I finished everything.
There are a lot of old clothes in my room.
Some I haven't worn in five years.
My wife says: sell them, or give them away.

tokens.en: to give (a gift); to see off

sentences.en: I say yes, but I still haven't done it.
Every piece has a story.
When I went out this morning the weather was lovely.
The sun was bright and there was little wind.
The trees by the road had all turned green.
I think spring has already come.
I didn't want to go to work, I wanted to walk outside.
My mom has a new phone.
She asks me a lot of questions.
I've shown her ten times and she still forgets.
I got a little impatient.
Then I thought: when I was little, she taught me to talk.
It rained hard that afternoon.
I had no umbrella, so I waited by the shop door.
Three other people were waiting too.
None of us spoke, we just watched the rain.

sentences.en: When the rain eased everyone left.
My grandfather is eighty this year.
Every morning he gets up at six and walks for an hour.
He says it keeps him healthy.
His eyes aren't great, but he still reads the paper.

tokens.en: to look at; to read; to watch

sentences.en: He says he wants to know what's happening out there.
I love buying books.
Last month I bought twelve.
But I only finished two.

tokens.en: to look at; to read; to watch

sentences.en: The new books are on the table and on the floor.
Today I went to the bookshop again.
I wanted to learn to cook Chinese food.
I watched it on my phone many times.

sentences.en: The first time, my dish was too salty.
The second time was better; the third was really good.
Now all my friends want to come eat at my place.
Every morning at six a woman runs past my door.
She runs when it rains too.
When it snows she still runs.
I don't know her, but I see her every day.
Last week she didn't come and I was a bit worried.
My first Chinese friend was called Xiao Bai.

sentences.en: We met on a train.
My Chinese was very poor then.
We talked for six hours.
We still call each other often.
Yesterday I finished my meal before realizing I'd left my wallet.
I was very embarrassed.

sentences.en: I wanted to call a friend, but my phone was dead too.
The waiter said: it's fine, come pay tomorrow.
This morning the first thing I did was go there.
My little brother is five and asks a lot of questions.
Why is the sky blue?
Do fish sleep?
I can't answer a lot of them.
So I've started reading too.

sentences.en: Our television is very old.
The color is off too — everyone's face is red.
Dad says we'll buy a new one next month.
He's been saying that for two years.
I think we'll keep using this one.
The first time I flew I was very frightened.
The old lady next to me noticed.
She said: don't be afraid, I've flown fifty times.
Then she talked with me the whole way.
By the time we landed I wasn't afraid any more.
Our school library is very quiet.
Students read and do problems in there.

sentences.en: I go three times a week.
There's a table there I like best.
It's by the door, with a big tree outside.
I don't like running, and I don't like basketball.
But I really like walking.
I walk for an hour every day.
When I walk I think about a lot of things.
I think that's exercise too.
Today I got a letter from my mom.
Everyone uses a phone now, but she still writes letters.
Her handwriting is big and slow.
The letter is all small things from home.
I read it three times.

passages.title: 我们班的新同学
passages.title_en: The New Student in Our Class

sentences.en: A new student joined our class.
On the first day he didn't talk to anyone.
At noon I asked him to eat with us.
He said he likes basketball too.
Now he's the most talkative person in our class.
When it was raining, a little cat was by my door.
It was small and cold.
I gave it a little milk.
It finished and left.
The next day it came again — now it lives with me.
Autumn is my favorite season.
Not cold, not hot, and the sky is very high.
The trees turn from green to yellow and red.
I like walking under those trees.
But autumn is very short.
My computer is seven years old.
It starts up very slowly.

sentences.en: Every morning I turn it on and then go make coffee.
By the time the coffee's ready, so is the computer.
I think that works out fine.
Every morning I walk my sister to school.

At the school gate she runs in.
She doesn't look back, but I watch her go in every time.

passages.title: 我不想长大
passages.title_en: I Don't Want to Grow Up

sentences.en: When I was little I wanted to grow up fast.
I thought grown-ups could do anything.
Now I'm a grown-up.
I can eat all the apples I want, but I'm busy every day.
Sometimes I want to go back to being a kid.
Nothing big happened today.
In the morning I had coffee and read the paper.

tokens.en: to look at; to read; to watch

sentences.en: At noon I ate with a colleague and we laughed a lot.
In the evening I read at home with the cat asleep beside me.

tokens.en: to look at; to read; to watch
